messages:
sara_cs: Sapphire reporting a sudden p95/p99 regression on text-gen — interactive UI timing out for some users. p95 ~1.8s -> 2.6s, p99 ~3.1s -> 4.8s starting ~15:12 UTC. Customer can repro consistently. Request id: req_saph_4f2b.

alex_oncall: Thanks Sara. Do we have the exact route + payload they used? Any config changes or deploys in the last hour?

sara_cs: Payload they shared (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b-chat-v2","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":512,"temperature":0.0}'
```
Customer says this hits high tail within ~2-3 requests. No config changes on their side.

observability-bot: Alert: route=/v1/generate region=us-west-2 model=rwd-13b-chat-v2 p95=2600ms p99=4820ms (5m window) — baseline p99 ~1200ms. [link to dashboard]

mike_engruntime: Looking at serving metrics — admission queue length for tenant=sapphire shot up around 15:10 UTC. Worker concurrency for that pool hit the hard limit (concurrency=64). We also see repeated KV-cache miss spikes and higher memcpy times.

mike_engruntime: Relevant logs (trimmed):
```
2026-03-16T15:10:18Z worker-12 WARN admit_queue: enqueue_len=78 concurrency=64 tenant=sapphire
2026-03-16T15:10:19Z worker-12 ERROR exec: failed_to_acquire_slot id=req_saph_4f2b reason=concurrency_limit
2026-03-16T15:11:02Z runtime PERF kv_cache: evict_rate=0.32 memcpy_ms=5.6
```

jenna_sre: Sounds like overloaded pool + transient KV thrash — backlog leading to queuing delays. Any recent kernel/quantization changes on that model?

mike_engruntime: We rolled a minor kernel optimization to the runtime earlier today (canary->prod) that changes the memcpy path on certain GPUs. Canary looked fine on unit tests but load-run wasn't representative. Looking at timing, memcpy_ms up correlates with the rollout window.

alex_oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) increase tenant concurrency cap for Sapphire (quick); 2) route Sapphire to dedicated spare pool we keep for emergencies; 3) rollback kernel optimization (slower path but stable). Which is fastest?

mike_engruntime: Fastest is to bump concurrency for that tenant and enable prefix caching TTL longer to reduce KV misses. Route change requires deploy-bot action but is low-risk. Rollback will take longer to verify.

jenna_sre: I can provision a temporary worker ramp for that pool (spin up 4 extra workers) — takes ~6-8 min. If we do concurrency bump + worker ramp + caching TTL increase, that should bring p99 down under 2s.

sara_cs: Customer ok with temporary changes. They requested ETA and will watch for improvement.

deploy-bot: policy-update: routing-rule(sapphire) -> emergency-dedicated-pool applied by jenna_sre at 15:23 UTC.

mike_engruntime: Increased tenant concurrency cap from 64 -> 96 for tenant=sapphire (temporary). Enabled extended prefix KV TTL for their model.

observability-bot: Update: after routing + concurrency bump p95=900ms p99=1700ms (3m window).

alex_oncall: Nice. Keep an eye on overall cluster utilization — we don't want cross-tenant regressions. Jenna, leave the emergency pool for 1 hour and then we reassess.

jenna_sre: Agreed. I'll monitor for the next 60m and post any anomalies. If stable, we'll gradually reduce the emergency allocations.

sara_cs: Passing update to customer: "We routed your traffic to a dedicated pool and temporarily increased concurrency; p99 has dropped significantly. We'll keep monitoring and follow up with root-cause."

mike_engruntime: Action items (short):
- Reproduce locally with loadtest using same payload + KV pattern
- Re-run canary with representative traffic
- Investigate memcpy regression in kernel change
- Plan either targeted fix or rollback

alex_oncall: Tagging this thread for postmortem if we find the kernel change caused the regression. For now, mitigating steps completed. :thumbsup:

sara_cs: Thanks everyone — I'll keep the customer updated.

jenna_sre: Monitoring dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/ingress/sapphire-emergency — I'll post follow-ups here.

mike_engruntime: If anyone needs the reproducer script, ping me and I'll drop it in the incident folder.

sara_cs: Closing loop with customer now. Will reopen if anything else crops up.
